messages:
Sam: Heads up — ran an nsys trace against the dedicated runtime to dig into the p95 latency spike for long sequences. The timeline has big idle gaps during the kernel-selection phase and I keep seeing CUPTI-related errors in the trace output. Pasting a clipped snippet below.

Sam: ```
nsys: Warning: CUPTI call cuptiActivityEnable failed: 0x5 (CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED)
nsys: Warning: Missing activity records for some kernels; timeline shows long 'kernel selection' idle regions (~20-80ms) between launches
KERNEL LAUNCH: aten_matmul: queued=1234 start=... end=... (missing)
KERNEL LAUNCH: kv_cache_read: queued=1240 start=... end=... (long gap)
```

Joan: Which nsys + driver combo are you running? We hit similar oddness last month when nsys + CUPTI activity were incompatible with the kernel driver version.

Sam: nsys 2024.1.0 (installed via apt), CUDA toolkit 12.2 in the image, driver on node is 530.41.03. The trace was taken from a container (K8s) running as non-root.

Ryan: Two quick checks: 1) try running nsys on the host (not inside container) to rule out container permission/namespace issues; 2) run with sudo or add the container cap for accessing CUPTI/device metrics — CUPTI sometimes needs extra privileges to attach.

Carla: Also try a trace with explicit traceset: `nsys profile --output=trace1 --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx python -m redwood.runtime.bench --seq 2048` — nvtx and explicit cuda tracing helped us surface kernel timings when CUPTI failed to emit activity.

Sam: Tried both suggestions. Host run shows fewer CUPTI warnings but still some kernels missing. Running `sudo nsys` reduced the warning frequency. Perfetto + nvplugin gave a separate timeline where kernel durations are present but the ordering looks different (kernel selection still highlighted as a hotspot).

perf-bot: Automated note: opened infra ticket #INF-4821 to trial driver upgrades on a canary pool.

Joan: Sounds like two separate issues colliding: (A) CUPTI/NSYS compatibility with driver (missing activity records), and (B) our kernel-selection loop/heuristics introducing real latency between launches. We should triage them independently.

Ryan: For (A) we should try: 1) upgrade drivers on one node to the latest stable NVIDIA driver (or test the vendor recommended combo for current nsys), 2) test with nsys 2023.x (downgrade) and 2024.x (upgrade) to see which direction helps. Document exact versions and trace outputs.

Carla: For (B) instrument the runtime with NVTX around the kernel-selection code path and KV cache lookup — that will let us see whether the time is spent doing CPU-side work (searching quantized index, lock contention, memory copies) vs waiting on device. Example insertion: `nvtx.range_push(\"kernel_select:shard-4\"); /* selection code */ nvtx.range_pop();`

Sam: Quick profiling note — when I enabled PERF events (perf record) on the host during a repro, we saw syscalls and futex waits clustered in the same window as the kernel-selection stalls. That suggests CPU-level blocking (locks or IO) rather than purely driver scheduling.

Joan: Good catch. Can you paste the perf top snippet? If it's futex/epoll/syscall heavy we should trace our batching queue and lock hold times.

Sam: ```
# perf top (top flame) snapshot during stall
  12.3%  redwood-runtime  [k] futex_wait
   9.8%  redwood-runtime  [.] _ZN10BatchQueue...lock_helper
   7.1%  libc.so.6        [.] __memcpy
   5.0%  driver           [k] nvhost_syncpt_read
```

Ryan: That lines up with the KV cache path doing memcpy + lock. My hunch: when sequence is long we hit a path that serializes cache reads which blocks the batch pipeline and increases the apparent idle between kernels.

Carla: Actionable plan:
- Sam: add NVTX spans around KV cache read + kernel selection and re-run nsys + perfetto on host (non-root then root) and attach logs to INF-4821.
- Ryan: add micro-bench for cache hit vs miss to measure memcpy/lock times under realistic concurrency.
- Joan/infra: try staging driver bump on one canary node and report whether CUPTI warnings disappear.

Sam: Will do. For the CUPTI warnings I also captured `NSYS_LOGS` output and saved the full `.qdrep`. Uploading to the ticket now. If infra cannot bump drivers quickly we may fallback to using perfetto+NVTX as our primary tracing path for these traces.

Carla: One more note — if anyone else tries this, avoid running nsys inside a CRI-O container without `--privileged` or proper device mounts; we've seen silent activity loss there.

Sam: Thanks — I'll post the results here when the canary runs complete. :thumbsup:
